sources: Luke 19:1-2 (Jesus passes through Jericho; Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector, and rich)
Luke 19:3-4 (he wanted to see Jesus, couldn’t because of the crowd, being short; ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree, i.e. a sycomore fig)
Luke 19:5 (“Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house”)
Luke 19:6-7 (he came down and received him joyfully; all grumbled, “He has gone in to lodge with a man who is a sinner”)
Luke 19:8 (“half of my goods I give to the poor… I restore four times as much”)
Luke 19:9-10 (“Today, salvation has come to this house, because he also is a son of Abraham… to seek and to save that which was lost”)
Exodus 22:1 (fourfold repayment for a stolen sheep) and Leviticus 6:1-5 / Numbers 5:6-7 (one who confesses repays plus a fifth), behind the four-times “why”
Tax collectors in Roman Judea collected for Rome and were widely seen as collaborators and overchargers
check: Teach line reads the story as grace: welcome first, change after. Some readers take Zacchaeus’s words in 19:8 as a description of what he already does; confirm the framing is acceptable.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? ever felt like people only see your worst?
options: i’m sorry. that’s heavy to carry. this story is for you.
most of us have. keep them in mind while you hear this one.
good. just listen. someone you know might need this one.

steps.line: Zacchaeus was the chief tax collector in the town of Jericho, and he was rich. Everyone knew how tax collectors got rich.

steps.q: Why did people dislike tax collectors so much back then?
o: They were Roman soldiers from abroad
They worked for Rome and skimmed extra
They kept the Temple’s offerings
steps.why: They gathered taxes for Rome, the power ruling the land, and kept the extra. To their neighbors, they were traitors.

steps.line: When Jesus came through town, Zacchaeus wanted to see him. But he was short, and the crowd wouldn’t let him through.

steps.q: So he runs ahead and climbs a tree. Jesus reaches it. What do you guess Jesus does?
o: Walks on; the crowd is waiting
Calls him down by name
Points him out to the crowd
steps.why: He stops, looks up, and uses his name. Nobody had introduced them.

steps.line: So he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree, to see Jesus pass by.
Jesus reached the tree, stopped and looked up. “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down. Today I must stay at your house.”
steps.label: Luke 19:5

steps.line: He hurried down and welcomed Jesus with joy. But the crowd grumbled, “He’s gone to stay with a sinner.”

steps.q: The whole town is grumbling. What does Zacchaeus do?
o: Argues with the crowd
Makes a promise about his money
Asks Jesus to leave quietly
steps.why: No one asked him to. He just stands up and says it.

steps.line: Zacchaeus stood up. “Look, Lord, half of what I own I’ll give to the poor. If I’ve cheated anyone, I’ll pay back four times as much.”
steps.label: Luke 19:8

steps.q: The law asked someone who owned up to cheating to repay it plus a fifth. Zacchaeus offers four times. What does that show?
o: He wanted to impress the crowd
His change was real, from the heart
A judge had ordered him to
steps.why: Nobody demanded it. He went far past what the law asked and chose the payback the law set for a thief.

steps.q: Zacchaeus is a Hebrew name. What does it mean?
o: Little one
Rich man
Pure, or innocent
steps.why: It comes from Zakkai: pure, innocent. The town’s biggest cheat had a name that meant clean, and by dinner he was living up to it.

steps.line: Jesus said, “Today salvation has come to this house, because he too is a son of Abraham. I came to seek and to save the lost.”
steps.label: Luke 19:9-10

steps.q: Jesus invited himself to dinner. Why would that hit the crowd so hard?
o: Sharing a meal meant accepting someone
Guests had to pay for their own food
Rabbis weren’t allowed in rich homes
steps.why: Eating at someone’s table said “we belong together.” Jesus chose the most hated table in Jericho, before Zacchaeus had changed a thing.

say: here’s what i love. jesus didn’t wait for zacchaeus to fix himself. he stopped under the tree and called him by name.
christians see it as a picture of grace: the welcome comes first, and the change follows.

steps.q: The crowd called him “a sinner.” Jesus called him “a son of Abraham.” What was Jesus saying?
o: He had to leave home, like Abraham
He still belonged to God’s family
It was a polite title for a rich man
steps.why: Abraham was the father of God’s people. The crowd had shut Zacchaeus out. Jesus said he still belonged.

today.say: jesus invited himself to dinner with a man the town had written off. today, reach out to someone like that: sit with them, invite them for coffee, or say one kind thing to them by name.
options: then you know where to start. one kind word, by name.
that’s how it started in jericho. someone looked up.
